site.name: OMUN
site.full_name: Oskar von Miller Model United Nations
site.description: OMUN is the Model United Nations conference of the Oskar-von-Miller-Gymnasium in Munich: students debate global issues as delegates of the UN member states.

home.hero_text: OMUN brings students from Munich and beyond to the Oskar-von-Miller-Gymnasium to debate, negotiate and draft resolutions as delegates of the United Nations.
home.about_text:
Model United Nations is a simulation of the United Nations. Every participant represents a member state in one of the committees, researches its position and argues for it: in speeches, in lobbying sessions and in the corridors.

OMUN is organised entirely by students of the Oskar-von-Miller-Gymnasium. Whether it is your first conference or your tenth, you will find a committee that suits you.

steps.title: Register
steps.text: Sign up on your own or as a school delegation. We assign countries and committees after the deadline.

steps.title: Prepare
steps.text: Read the study guide of your committee, research your country's position and write a position paper.

steps.title: Debate
steps.text: Give speeches, lobby for support, merge draft resolutions and vote them through the committee.

home.quote: Diplomacy is the art of letting someone else have your way.
home.cta_text: Registration is open until the deadline. Places in each committee are limited.

conference.motto: Rebuilding Trust in a Divided World
conference.intro: OMUN takes place over three days at the Oskar-von-Miller-Gymnasium in Munich-Schwabing. Below you find the preliminary programme. Details may still change; the final version is published in the delegate booklet.
conference.body:
## Dress code
Western business attire is expected during all sessions.

## Laptops
Please bring a laptop or tablet to write clauses and amendments. Wi-Fi is available on site.

## Getting here
The school is a short walk from the U-Bahn station *Münchner Freiheit* (U3/U6).

registration.intro: Fill in the form to register for OMUN. School delegations: please register every delegate individually and give the same school name. You will receive your country and committee allocation by e-mail after the deadline.
registration.closed_message: Registration is currently closed. Follow us on Instagram to find out when it opens.
registration.success_message: Thank you! We have received your registration and will be in touch by e-mail.

committees.name: General Assembly First Committee
topics: Preventing an arms race in outer space
committees.summary: The GA1 deals with disarmament and international security. A good first committee for new delegates.
committees.description: The First Committee of the General Assembly (Disarmament and International Security) considers all disarmament and security questions within the scope of the UN Charter.

committees.name: Human Rights Council
topics: Protecting privacy in the age of mass surveillance
committees.summary: The HRC promotes and protects human rights around the world.

committees.name: UN Environment Programme
topics: Financing the transition away from fossil fuels
committees.summary: UNEP sets the global environmental agenda.

committees.name: World Health Organization
committees.summary: The WHO directs and coordinates international health within the UN system.

committees.name: Economic and Social Council
topics: Regulating artificial intelligence in the labour market
committees.summary: ECOSOC coordinates the economic and social work of the UN.

committees.name: Security Council
topics: The situation in the Sahel region
Maritime security in the Red Sea
committees.summary: Fifteen members, five vetoes. For experienced delegates only.

news.title: Registration for OMUN 2027 is open
news.excerpt: Registration for the next conference is now open. Committees and topics are online.
news.body:
Registration for OMUN 2027 is now open. Have a look at the committees and their topics, then sign up via the registration form.

Study guides will be published here in the coming weeks.

faq.question: Do I need any MUN experience?
faq.answer: No. Committees marked *Beginner* are made for first-time delegates, and the chairs will explain the rules of procedure at the start.

faq.question: Which language is spoken?
faq.answer: All sessions are held in English.

faq.question: Who can take part?
faq.answer: Students from grade 9 upwards, from our own school and from other schools.

faq.question: What is a position paper?
faq.answer: A one-page summary of your country's position on the committee topic. Your study guide explains what it should contain.

faq.question: Can I choose my country?
faq.answer: You can state preferences in the registration form. We try to take them into account, but cannot guarantee them.
